topic: Forms with PHP and data validation; preventing injection
title: Server-side validation and output escaping
instructions:
## Never trust the request

A registration form posts `username`, `email`, `password` and `confirm`. Write the server-side logic (the course uses PHP; the same functions exist there as `htmlspecialchars` and `filter_var`).

1. `escapeHtml(text)`: replace `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` with `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`, in that order of safety (ampersand first).
2. `validateRegistration(form)`: return an **array of error messages** (empty when valid): `"username must be 3-20 letters, digits or underscores"`, `"email is invalid"` (must contain `@` and a dot after it), `"password must be at least 8 characters"`, `"passwords do not match"`.
3. `safeSql(username)`: return the parameterised query and its parameters as an object `{ sql: "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ?", params: [username] }`. Never put the value into the string.
hints: Replace & first, or the entities you add will be escaped again.
The username rule is the regular expression /^[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,20}$/.
Prepared statements send the SQL and the values separately; that is why the ? placeholder is the whole defence against SQL injection.

expected: username must be 3-20 letters, digits or underscores
password must be at least 8 characters

checks.label: safeSql keeps the value out of the query
checks.name: safeSql

realityNote: In PHP: htmlspecialchars($s, ENT_QUOTES), filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL), and $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ?")->execute([$username]). The error list pattern maps directly onto the messages shown next to each field.
